options.a: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law
options.b: Obtain the highest possible price even when the seller directs a quicker sale
options.c: Treat buyer and seller with equal advocacy so both receive fair representation
options.d: Advise the seller on title and tax matters as the seller's legal representative

distractorExplanations.b: Price is not the top duty; obedience requires following the seller's lawful instruction to favor a quick sale.
distractorExplanations.c: Equal advocacy describes a neutral or dual role; a listing broker owes loyalty to the seller client, not both sides.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses agency with legal practice; a broker must refer title and tax questions to an attorney or CPA.

options.a: At closing, when the settlement agent reviews the final agency paperwork
options.b: Before or as soon as practicable when the dual/designated relationship arises
options.c: Once the purchase contract is accepted and both parties have signed it
options.d: Only if one of the parties is an existing client rather than a customer

distractorExplanations.a: Closing is far too late; informed consent must come before the licensee acts for both parties.
distractorExplanations.c: Waiting until acceptance means both parties negotiated without knowing the licensee's divided loyalty.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosure is triggered by the dual or designated relationship itself, not by whether a party was a prior client.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agency disclosure timing is early—when the dual or designated relationship is created or contemplated. Exact timing follows the applicable license-law rules.

options.a: The listing broker is owed a commission unless the seller personally finds the buyer during the term
options.b: The seller may list with several brokers and pays a commission only to the broker who procures the buyer
options.c: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer
options.d: The broker keeps any sale proceeds above the seller's stated minimum price as the commission

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where the seller keeps the right to sell without owing a commission.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes an open listing, where only the procuring broker is paid and the seller may also sell directly.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a net listing, which concerns how the commission is calculated, not exclusivity of the right to sell.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell typically protects the listing broker's commission if a sale occurs during the listing term. The exact protection follows the terms of the listing agreement.

options.a: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
options.b: The seller's reasons for selling and the lowest price the seller is willing to accept
options.c: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood surrounding the property
options.d: That a former occupant of the home was living with HIV or AIDS

distractorExplanations.b: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts.
distractorExplanations.c: Discussing neighborhood racial or religious composition is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: HIV/AIDS is a protected disability under federal fair housing law; it is not a material property fact to disclose.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared; confidential motivations may be protected. Disclosure duties follow applicable law.

options.a: Suggest an offer amount, since helping the buyer also helps close the sale
options.b: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role
options.c: Share the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer can offer efficiently
options.d: Give a price opinion as long as the buyer has signed the agency disclosure form

distractorExplanations.a: Recommending an offer amount is buyer advocacy that conflicts with the listing agent's loyalty to the seller.
distractorExplanations.c: Revealing the seller's bottom line breaches the confidentiality duty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.d: Signing an agency disclosure does not create buyer representation; the agent still represents only the seller.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift/disclosure. If allowed, the brokerage may properly create buyer agency with required disclosures.

options.a: Lacked consideration or a legal purpose
options.b: Made only an oral agreement to buy land
options.c: Was induced by fraud or was a minor
options.d: Later found a better deal on another home

distractorExplanations.a: A contract missing consideration or a legal purpose is void or unenforceable, not voidable at one party's option.
distractorExplanations.b: An oral land contract is unenforceable under the statute of frauds, which differs from being voidable.
distractorExplanations.d: Buyer's remorse is not a legal ground; a valid contract cannot be avoided because a better deal appears.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party. Whether the contract is voidable depends on the circumstances.

options.a: Deadlines are targets, and a party may perform within a reasonable time after
options.b: The closing date is binding, but contingency deadlines may be extended freely
options.c: The contract must close within 30 days of acceptance to remain enforceable
options.d: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach

distractorExplanations.a: That is the reasonable-time standard that applies when the clause is absent; the clause makes dates strict.
distractorExplanations.b: The clause applies to all contract dates, including contingency deadlines, not just the closing date.
distractorExplanations.c: The clause enforces the dates the parties chose; it does not impose a fixed 30-day closing period.

options.a: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price, creating conflict-of-interest concerns
options.b: The broker's commission is a fixed percentage of the sale price, creating price-fixing concerns under antitrust law
options.c: The seller nets less because the commission is deducted before the seller's mortgage payoff at closing
options.d: The broker must guarantee the seller's net price, creating personal liability if the home sells for less

distractorExplanations.b: Confuses net listings with antitrust price fixing; a percentage commission is not a net listing at all.
distractorExplanations.c: The order of payoffs on the closing statement is not the issue; the conflict comes from the broker keeping the excess.
distractorExplanations.d: A net listing does not make the broker guarantee the seller's figure; the risk is the broker's incentive to underprice.

options.a: An obligation to purchase on stated terms by a set date, once consideration is paid
options.b: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period, usually for consideration
options.c: A right of first refusal to match any third-party offer the owner later accepts
options.d: Equitable title to the property from signing, as under an installment land contract

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses an option with a bilateral purchase contract; the optionee may buy but is not obligated to.
distractorExplanations.c: A right of first refusal depends on a third-party offer; an option lets the optionee buy on fixed terms at will.
distractorExplanations.d: Equitable title arises under a contract for deed or sales contract; an optionee holds only a contract right.

options.a: A misstatement of a measurable fact, such as square footage, made without intent
options.b: A seller's silence about a known latent defect that a buyer could not discover
options.c: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty
options.d: Advertising that omits the brokerage name, making it a blind ad under license law

distractorExplanations.a: A false measurable fact is negligent misrepresentation even without intent; puffing is only opinion or hype.
distractorExplanations.b: Silence about a known latent defect is concealment or nondisclosure, not exaggerated opinion.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a blind ad, a license-law advertising violation unrelated to exaggerated sales talk.

options.a: Practicing law whenever they complete any blank on a standard purchase form
options.b: Acting as the escrow agent and must hold the earnest money until closing
options.c: Required to have the buyer's attorney approve each blank before signing
options.d: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms

distractorExplanations.a: Filling blanks on approved forms is generally permitted; it becomes law practice when drafting new legal clauses.
distractorExplanations.b: Completing a form does not make the licensee an escrow agent; who holds earnest money is set by the contract.
distractorExplanations.c: Attorney review may be recommended, but there is no general rule requiring attorney approval of each blank.

options.a: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal
options.b: Proceed as a dual agent after giving the buyer written notice of the relationship
options.c: Switch to representing the buyer while keeping the seller's listing active for both
options.d: Terminate the listing agreement unilaterally and refund the seller's marketing costs

distractorExplanations.b: Dual agency requires informed consent from both parties; notice to the buyer alone cannot replace the seller's consent.
distractorExplanations.c: Representing the buyer while still holding the listing is undisclosed dual agency, the exact thing the seller refused.
distractorExplanations.d: Refusing dual agency does not let the broker abandon the listing; the broker simply declines to represent the buyer.

options.a: Using client trust money for the broker's own business or personal expenses
options.b: Depositing several clients' earnest money deposits into one trust account
options.c: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds improperly
options.d: Holding earnest money beyond the deadline for depositing it into escrow

distractorExplanations.a: Spending trust money on the broker's own expenses is conversion, a separate and more serious violation.
distractorExplanations.b: Pooling multiple clients' funds in one properly kept trust account is permitted; mixing in broker money is not.
distractorExplanations.d: Late deposit is a timeliness violation of trust-account rules, not the mixing of trust and personal funds.

options.a: Inheritance
options.b: Homestead
options.c: Reversion
options.d: Survivorship

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses joint tenancy with tenancy in common; a joint tenant's interest passes to co-owners, not heirs.
distractorExplanations.b: Homestead is a separate protection of a residence from certain creditors, not a feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.c: Reversion is the grantor's future interest after a life estate, unrelated to co-ownership rights.

options.a: Public use and the owner's written consent
options.b: Just compensation set by the county assessor
options.c: Public use/purpose and just compensation
options.d: A court finding that the owner is delinquent on taxes

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is the government's power to take without consent; only just compensation is owed to the owner.
distractorExplanations.b: Compensation is fair market value set by negotiation or the court, not the assessor's tax value; public use is also required.
distractorExplanations.d: Tax delinquency leads to a tax sale, a different process; eminent domain needs public use and compensation.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public purpose and just compensation under the Constitution. This framework comes from the Fifth Amendment.

options.a: Upon the death of the remainderman
options.b: When the life tenant conveys the interest
options.c: When the life tenant stops occupying it
options.d: Upon the death of the measuring life

distractorExplanations.a: The remainderman's death does not end the estate; the remainder passes to the remainderman's heirs.
distractorExplanations.b: A life tenant may convey the interest, creating a life estate pur autre vie that still ends at the original tenant's death.
distractorExplanations.c: Occupancy is not required; the life tenant may lease the property and the estate continues for the measuring life.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Life estates are measured by a life; remainder/reversion follows. The estate's terms may define the measuring life differently.

options.a: A zoning variance that permits a nonconforming use of the lot
options.b: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability
options.c: The legal action used to clear disputed claims from a title
options.d: Constructive notice given by recording a deed in public records

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses land-use regulation with title; a variance is a zoning permission, not a claim against ownership.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a quiet title action, which removes a cloud rather than being the cloud itself.
distractorExplanations.d: Recording gives constructive notice that protects title; it is not a defect impairing marketability.

options.a: Must acquire title at the same time and through the same deed
options.b: Hold a right of survivorship so a deceased owner's share passes to the others
options.c: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship unless specified
options.d: Need consent of all co-owners before selling their own share

distractorExplanations.a: Unity of time and title are joint tenancy requirements; tenants in common may acquire at different times.
distractorExplanations.b: Survivorship is the hallmark of joint tenancy; a tenant in common's share passes to heirs or devisees.
distractorExplanations.d: A tenant in common may sell an undivided share without the other co-owners' consent.

options.a: A rezoning of the entire district by amending the zoning map
options.b: Permission for a use the ordinance lists as allowed after special review
options.c: A use that predates the ordinance and may continue as nonconforming
options.d: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship

distractorExplanations.a: Amending the zoning map is rezoning, a legislative act; a variance grants relief for one parcel.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes a conditional or special use permit, not relief from a requirement due to hardship.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a legal nonconforming (grandfathered) use, not a variance granted by the zoning board.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases. The variance is granted by the zoning authority.

options.a: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.b: Having the grantor's signature notarized
options.c: Delivering the signed deed to the grantee
options.d: Purchasing an owner's title insurance policy

distractorExplanations.b: Acknowledgment makes a deed eligible for recording but by itself gives no notice to the public.
distractorExplanations.c: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties; recording is what gives notice to the world.
distractorExplanations.d: Title insurance protects the insured against covered defects; it does not give public notice of the deed.

options.a: Land bordering a lake, sea, or ocean with still or tidal water
options.b: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream
options.c: Rights to minerals, oil, and gas beneath the land's surface
options.d: Rights to use the airspace above the land for development

distractorExplanations.a: Rights along lakes, seas, and oceans are littoral rights; riparian rights concern flowing rivers and streams.
distractorExplanations.c: Subsurface mineral rights are a separate bundle of rights and are unrelated to water boundaries.
distractorExplanations.d: Air rights cover space above the land and can be severed, but they are not water rights.

options.a: 1% of the purchase price
options.b: 1% of the down payment
options.c: 1% of the interest rate
options.d: 1% of the loan amount

distractorExplanations.a: Points are based on the loan amount, not the price; with a down payment the loan is smaller than the price.
distractorExplanations.b: The down payment is the buyer's equity, not the base for points; points are 1% of the amount borrowed.
distractorExplanations.c: A point is a fee on the loan amount; it may buy down the rate but is not computed from the rate.

options.a: Interest each month, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.b: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term
options.c: Principal only, with interest added to the balance each month
options.d: Interest and principal in payments that increase each year of the term

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an interest-only or straight term loan with a balloon, not a fully amortizing loan.
distractorExplanations.c: Adding unpaid interest to the balance is negative amortization, the opposite of an amortizing payment.
distractorExplanations.d: Rising payments describe a graduated payment mortgage; a fixed-rate amortizing payment stays level.

options.a: Requiring lenders to disclose the APR and finance charge before consummation
options.b: Prohibiting lending discrimination based on race, sex, age, or marital status
options.c: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures
options.d: Requiring a three-day right to rescind on every purchase-money mortgage

distractorExplanations.a: APR and finance charge disclosure come from the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not RESPA.
distractorExplanations.b: That is the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, which bars credit discrimination; RESPA targets settlement practices.
distractorExplanations.d: The TILA three-day rescission right applies to certain refinances and home-equity loans, not purchase-money loans.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures (with TRID integration for many loans). These rules apply in covered residential transactions.

options.a: Lets the lender demand full payoff if the property is sold
options.b: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early
options.c: Lets the lender accelerate the full balance after a borrower default
options.d: Charges a fee when the borrower's monthly payment arrives late

distractorExplanations.a: That is a due-on-sale (alienation) clause, which is triggered by a transfer rather than an early payoff.
distractorExplanations.c: That is an acceleration clause, which is triggered by default rather than by voluntary early payoff.
distractorExplanations.d: That is a late-payment charge; a prepayment penalty applies when the borrower pays early, not late.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Prepayment penalties charge for early payoff when permitted by the loan terms and law. The penalty applies only when the note and law allow it.

options.a: An FHA loan is used with a down payment of 3.5%
options.b: A VA loan is used with no down payment at all
options.c: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)
options.d: Conventional LTV falls to 78% of original value

distractorExplanations.a: FHA loans carry the government's mortgage insurance premium (MIP), not private mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.b: VA loans are guaranteed by the VA and do not require PMI even with no down payment; a funding fee applies instead.
distractorExplanations.d: 78% of original value is when borrower-paid PMI terminates under the Homeowners Protection Act, not when it starts.

options.a: Can adjust based on the margin alone, while the index stays fixed
options.b: Is fixed for the term but the payment rises with property taxes
options.c: Can adjust based on the lender's discretion, without any rate caps
options.d: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps

distractorExplanations.a: Reversed: the margin is the fixed part of an ARM; the index is the market rate that moves.
distractorExplanations.b: Payment changes from escrowed taxes affect fixed-rate loans too; that does not make a rate adjustable.
distractorExplanations.c: ARM changes are tied to a published index plus margin, and periodic and lifetime caps limit them.

options.a: Covered title defects and claims against ownership
options.b: Loss to the lender if the borrower defaults on the loan
options.c: Physical damage to the home from fire or other hazards
options.d: Title defects that arise after the policy's effective date

distractorExplanations.b: Default risk is covered by mortgage insurance (PMI or FHA MIP), not by title insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: Fire and similar casualty losses are covered by hazard (homeowner's) insurance, not title insurance.
distractorExplanations.d: Title policies cover defects existing at or before the policy date; later-arising problems are excluded.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Owner's/lender's title policies insure against covered title risks, not casualty. Coverage depends on the terms of the owner's or lender's policy.

options.a: The buyer is credited; it reduces cash needed
options.b: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed
options.c: The item is split evenly between buyer and seller
options.d: The lender pays it; it reduces the loan amount

distractorExplanations.a: Reverses the entries: a credit reduces what the buyer owes, while a debit is a charge to the buyer.
distractorExplanations.c: Splits are prorations or negotiated sharing, shown as separate debits to each party, not the meaning of a debit.
distractorExplanations.d: A buyer debit is a charge to the buyer; lender-paid items appear as credits, and the loan amount is unchanged.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. For the seller, a debit reduces sale proceeds.

options.a: Originate loans directly to borrowers through banks and mortgage brokers
options.b: Insure lenders against borrower default on high-LTV conventional loans
options.c: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity for originators
options.d: Set the federal funds rate and reserve requirements for lenders

distractorExplanations.a: Origination happens in the primary mortgage market; the secondary market buys loans after they are made.
distractorExplanations.b: Default insurance on high-LTV conventional loans is private mortgage insurance, not the secondary market.
distractorExplanations.d: Monetary policy tools belong to the Federal Reserve, not to secondary market investors such as Fannie Mae.

options.a: Disclosure of the APR and finance charges to consumer borrowers
options.b: Lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status
options.c: Fees for referring settlement services in residential loans
options.d: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans

distractorExplanations.a: Credit cost disclosure is the Truth in Lending Act; usury laws cap the rate itself.
distractorExplanations.b: Credit discrimination is governed by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, not usury laws.
distractorExplanations.c: Referral fees and kickbacks for settlement services are restricted by RESPA, not usury laws.

options.a: Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
options.b: Finance construction draws as a new home is built, then convert to a permanent loan
options.c: Combine a first and second mortgage to avoid PMI on an 80/10/10 purchase
options.d: Let a buyer take over the seller's existing loan on its original terms

distractorExplanations.b: That describes a construction (construction-to-permanent) loan, which funds building rather than a sale gap.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a piggyback loan structure used to avoid PMI, not short-term gap financing between homes.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a loan assumption, where the buyer takes over the seller's mortgage, not a bridge loan.

options.a: They let the broker withdraw earned interest without client consent
options.b: They let the broker move surplus trust funds into operating accounts
options.c: They determine each agent's share of the commission split
options.d: They help detect shortages/overages and demonstrate compliance

distractorExplanations.a: Reconciliation does not authorize withdrawals; trust interest is disbursed only as statute or the agreement allows.
distractorExplanations.b: Surplus trust money is not broker money; moving it into operating accounts would be conversion.
distractorExplanations.c: Commission splits come from the broker-agent agreement; reconciliation compares trust ledgers to bank records.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-ak-licens.explanation: Regular reconciliation is a core trust-account control. Reconciliation records support compliance reviews by the state commission.

options.a: May be required or strongly expected, but does not excuse license law violations
options.b: Covers fines imposed by the Alaska Real Estate Commission for violations
options.c: Protects the buyer against title defects found after closing
options.d: Covers intentional misrepresentation if the licensee acted for the client

distractorExplanations.b: E&O policies cover negligence claims, not regulatory fines; discipline by the commission is still the licensee's.
distractorExplanations.c: Title defects are covered by title insurance, not the licensee's E&O policy.
distractorExplanations.d: E&O excludes intentional or fraudulent acts; it covers negligent errors, not deliberate misstatements.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-ak-licens.explanation: E&O manages negligence risk; it is not a license to violate the law. Firm and commission risk practices shape E&O requirements.

options.a: May negotiate offer terms if the supervising broker reviews and approves them afterward
options.b: Performs administrative tasks under supervision and must not negotiate unless licensed
options.c: May show property and discuss price unsupervised once trained by the firm
options.d: Performs licensed tasks under a broker's supervision without needing a license

distractorExplanations.a: Negotiating is licensed activity; after-the-fact broker approval does not let an unlicensed coordinator negotiate.
distractorExplanations.c: Showing property and discussing price are licensed activities; firm training does not replace a license.
distractorExplanations.d: Supervision does not authorize unlicensed people to perform licensed activities; only clerical tasks are allowed.

options.a: Permitted if the ad shows the licensee's license number
options.b: Permitted on social media but not in print advertising
options.c: Allowed for team ads without the firm name
options.d: Noncompliant with brokerage identification rules

distractorExplanations.a: A license number does not replace the required brokerage name; ads must identify the responsible firm.
distractorExplanations.b: Brokerage identification rules apply to online and social media ads just as they do to print.
distractorExplanations.c: Team advertising must still identify the sponsoring brokerage; a team name alone is not enough.

options.a: Refuse to conceal legally required disclosures
options.b: Comply, since the seller alone signs the disclosure form
options.c: Disclose it only if a buyer asks a direct question
options.d: Leave the defect to the home inspector

distractorExplanations.b: The licensee has an independent duty to disclose known material defects; the seller signing the form does not shift it.
distractorExplanations.c: Known material latent defects must be disclosed proactively, not only in answer to a buyer's question.
distractorExplanations.d: Relying on a buyer's inspection does not excuse concealing a known latent defect the licensee must disclose.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-ak-licens.explanation: Licensees cannot participate in fraud; illegal instructions must be refused. If the seller persists, the licensee should consider withdrawing from the listing.

options.a: Shifts liability for agents' violations from the broker to the agents
options.b: Documents supervision standards and compliant procedures for affiliated licensees
options.c: Takes the place of required continuing education for affiliated licensees
options.d: Satisfies the broker's supervision duty without any further review of agents' files

distractorExplanations.a: A manual does not transfer the broker's supervisory liability; the broker remains responsible for supervision.
distractorExplanations.c: Continuing education is a separate licensing requirement that a policy manual cannot replace.
distractorExplanations.d: A written manual supports but does not satisfy supervision; brokers must still actively review transactions.

options.a: Operate under the main office license with no separate supervision
options.b: Use a separate trade name from the main office
options.c: Be registered/comply with branch office rules when required
options.d: Be licensed as separate brokerages with their own owners

distractorExplanations.a: Branches still need supervision by a responsible broker or manager; a main-office license alone is not enough.
distractorExplanations.b: A branch must operate under the firm's licensed name; a separate trade name can mislead consumers.
distractorExplanations.d: A branch is part of the same brokerage, not a separately owned firm with its own broker license.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-ak-licens.explanation: Branch locations often need registration and supervision. Branches also need proper broker supervision.

options.a: Acceptable puffing because it states an opinion of results
options.b: Lawful if the brokerage name appears in the advertisement
options.c: Acceptable if the claim appears only on the firm's website
options.d: Likely deceptive unless substantiated and carefully qualified

distractorExplanations.a: A measurable performance claim (20% above market) is a factual claim, not opinion puffing.
distractorExplanations.b: Brokerage identification is a separate rule; naming the firm does not cure an unsubstantiated claim.
distractorExplanations.c: Advertising rules apply to websites just as to print; online placement does not excuse a deceptive claim.

options.a: What services a listing broker must still provide even in limited-service listings
options.b: The minimum commission rate a listing broker may charge in a limited-service listing
options.c: Which brokerage services an unlicensed assistant may perform
options.d: The disclosures a broker must give before acting as a dual agent

distractorExplanations.b: Statutes do not set commission rates; fixing minimum commissions would raise antitrust problems.
distractorExplanations.c: Unlicensed assistant rules are separate; minimum-service laws set duties owed by the listing broker.
distractorExplanations.d: Dual agency disclosure is a separate agency rule, not the core duties required in limited-service listings.

options.a: Disclose it, since the duty of confidentiality ends when the transaction closes
options.b: Protect confidential client information and not disclose without authority
options.c: Disclose it, because the buyer was a party to the same transaction
options.d: Refer the buyer to the cooperating agent, who may share it freely

distractorExplanations.a: Confidentiality can survive closing for non-public personal information; it does not end automatically at closing.
distractorExplanations.c: Being a party to the deal gives the buyer no right to the seller's personal contact information.
distractorExplanations.d: Passing the request to another agent does not make disclosure permissible; the information stays confidential.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-ak-licens.explanation: Confidentiality can survive closing for non-public personal information. Disclosure is allowed only with authority or a legal requirement.

options.a: A civil fine issued by the Alaska Division of Insurance
options.b: Discipline only by the local MLS, not the state
options.c: Prosecution by the FTC rather than state license action
options.d: Disciplinary action by Alaska Real Estate Commission

distractorExplanations.a: The Division of Insurance regulates insurers; the Alaska Real Estate Commission disciplines real estate licensees.
distractorExplanations.b: MLS sanctions are private; deceptive advertising is also a license-law violation the commission can discipline.
distractorExplanations.c: Federal law does not displace state license discipline; the commission acts on licensees' deceptive ads.
